tagline: From a wagon-train resupply post to cabins for Lincoln Highway motorists
intro: Bridger Valley Historic Byway follows paved roads through Fort Bridger, Urie and Lyman on the I-80 Business Loop. The Wyoming Transportation Commission adopted it into the state’s Scenic Byways and Backways Program. WYDOT describes that program as a way to combine travel with appreciation and protection of the state’s scenic, historic and cultural resources.

Jim Bridger and Louis Vasquez established a trading post here to serve travelers heading west. Its blacksmith shop offered travelers a service even when supplies and prices drew complaints. The valley subsequently carried the Pony Express, transcontinental railroad and Lincoln Highway. In 1925, the Black and Orange Cabins opened beside the fort to accommodate automobile travelers on the Lincoln Highway.
Traveling east through the valley, the business loop connects Fort Bridger, Urie and Lyman. At Urie, a spur runs south to Mountain View; another spur leads north to the old railroad town of Carter.

moments.title: Fort Bridger
moments.text: The trading post at Fort Bridger is a reconstruction. Jim Bridger and Louis Vasquez established the original post, which became a resupply point for wagon trains on the Oregon, California and Mormon trails. In an 1843 letter to Pierre Chouteau Jr., Bridger described a blacksmith shop and a supply of iron on the emigrants’ road. The U.S. Army established a military post here in 1858 and finally closed it in 1890. The site and remaining buildings passed to Wyoming’s Historical Landmark Commission in 1928. The old Pony Express barn and Mormon protective wall survive at the historic fort.

moments.title: Black and Orange Cabins
moments.text: The Black and Orange Cabins beside Fort Bridger served a later generation of travelers: motorists on the Lincoln Highway. Built in 1925, the tourist lodging operated until 1936. A sale in 1941 brought new ownership, but the cabins likely never reopened. The property then remained essentially abandoned from 1948 to 1996. The Fort Bridger Historical Society bought it in 1996 and donated it to the state. Wyoming began restoring the cabins in 2007, stabilizing foundations and repairing chimneys and roofs. That round of restoration ended in June 2009.

moments.title: Lyman
moments.text: Lyman is one of the towns on the byway’s I-80 Business Loop. It also has a connection to astronomy: the privately owned Mountain Skies Observatory is located here and used by the Bridger Valley Astronomical Society.
